name: Bergen Airport, Flesland
before:
Norway's second busiest airport, at Flesland in Bergen, with 6,306,623 passengers in 2018. The route to Oslo Gardermoen is among the busiest in Europe, and there is substantial helicopter traffic out to the North Sea oil platforms.

Two things to warn a client about. The main terminal has reached its capacity for simultaneous passengers, with security, check-in, the arrivals hall and baggage handling all short of space, so allow extra time at peak. And every passenger on an international flight has to pass through the duty free shop to reach their gate, with only limited exceptions.

The Bergen Light Rail was extended to the airport in April 2017, which is the easy way into the city, and a new terminal opened in August 2017.

SAS, Norwegian and Widerøe are the largest airlines here.

The airport opened on 2 October 1955, financed largely through NATO funds, and until the 1980s it was the Norwegian airport SAS used for intercontinental flights to New York.
after:
Norway's second busiest airport, at Flesland in Bergen, with more than 6.5 million passengers in 2025. There is also substantial helicopter traffic out to the North Sea oil platforms.

The Bergen Light Rail was extended to the airport in April 2017, giving a direct line to the city centre. A new terminal opened in August 2017.

SAS, Norwegian and Widerøe are the largest airlines here.

The airport opened on 2 October 1955, financed largely through NATO funds.

claims.note: SNL states it outright (article updated 6 February 2025). Avinor's 2025 table is the current check: Bergen is second to Oslo, ahead of Trondheim and Stavanger, and Avinor's other airports are grouped as regional airports with 11.2 million passengers between them.

claims.claim: Oslo route among the busiest in Europe
claims.wasBefore: The route to Oslo Gardermoen is among the busiest in Europe
claims.why: Wikipedia rests it on a 2007 ranking. No current second source found.

claims.claim: two things to warn a client about
claims.wasBefore: Two things to warn a client about.
claims.why: Goes with the two warnings below, both cut.

claims.wasBefore: The main terminal has reached its capacity for simultaneous passengers, with security, check-in, the arrivals hall and baggage handling all short of space, so allow extra time at peak.
claims.why: Out of date. It describes the 1988 terminal. SNL says that terminal was built for 2.8 million passengers a year, was overtaken, and was replaced by a new terminal opened on 17 August 2017 and built for up to 7.6 million.

claims.claim: international passengers must walk through the duty free shop
claims.wasBefore: And every passenger on an international flight has to pass through the duty free shop to reach their gate, with only limited exceptions.
claims.why: Wikipedia's account of the old terminal, sourced to 2012 press reports. No current second source for the 2017 terminal.

claims.claim: the light rail is the easy way into the city
claims.wasBefore: which is the easy way into the city
claims.why: A judgement, and not clear-cut: SNL puts the light rail at about 40 minutes from the centre, while Avinor puts the airport bus at about 20 minutes to the bus station. Replaced by the plain fact of a direct line.

claims.claim: until the 1980s SAS flew to New York from Bergen
claims.wasBefore: until the 1980s it was the Norwegian airport SAS used for intercontinental flights to New York
claims.why: Sources disagree on the dates. Wikipedia says until the 1980s; the Bergen byleksikon puts Bergen's time as Scandinavia's transatlantic gateway at the 1960s to the early 1970s, and names no airline.
